name: Remo of the Moa river
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress
sweep_summary: Remo of the Moa river (remo1248, Panoan, extinct) is not in the catalog. Both works with stress in the title are the same work, DeArmond 1976 'Proto-Gutob-Remo-Gtaq stressed monosyllabic vowels and initial consonants' (Austroasiatic Studies, Oceanic Linguistics Special Publication 13, pp. 213-228), which Glottolog lists twice (refs 121721, 54947) and links to remo1248 only because of the name 'Remo'. An open scan was downloaded from the SEAlang SALA archive and saved, p.1 scanned); its first paragraph says it reconstructs a 'South Munda language presumably once spoken in Orissa Province of India' (Gutob, Bonda/Remo bond1245, Gta'). Relevance: other language; priority none. No stress statement for the Panoan Remo exists: the only documentation is the Loos 1973-1974 SIL wordlists (already held by the project, accent marks on forms, no prose on placement), per Fleck 2013. updated with the new file and the misattribution note.

sources.note: Nothing. Two salvage wordlists (70 items handwritten 1973 from Ernesto Baquinahua; 81 items typed 1974 from Manuel Chomo, both Capanahua speakers recalling Remo of the Rio Môa from c. 1933). Forms carry impressionistic acute accents (e.g. sirí 'papaya', hóbo' 'casa', mahá' 'carachama', náwa' 'huangana', wïstí 'uno', rabí 'dos', mápo 'cabeza') but the only prose is an informant note (p.[3]), three segmental correspondences (p.[7]: k > glottal stop; Cap. š ~ Remo h; Cap. y- ~ Remo n-) and a 1974 header (p.[8]); no statement on stress/accent placement. Loos warns the data are suspect and Capanah…
